title: Hud and his people
hookLine: Hud tells 'Ad to ask forgiveness and He'll add strength to strength (11:52)
last: IN HIS NAME IT SAILS AND ANCHORS.

lines: THE HARDEST THING FOR THE STRONG.
cards: You've met the people of 'Ad before, in al-A'raf: the tower builders of ancient Arabia, proud of their strength, and the prophet sent from among them, Hud. Surah Hud carries his name and gives his preaching more room.
Here is a man standing up in a town where everyone is bigger, richer and louder than he is. They have wealth, fortresses, numbers; he has nothing they need.
And he tells them that the way to grow even stronger is to do the one thing strong people find hardest.

teach.b: Hud begins the way Nuh began before him in this surah: my people, worship God; you have no god but Him. I ask you no wage for this, he says; my wage is only from the One who made me.
Then something that sounds almost like a business proposal, in verse fifty-two, in paraphrase: my people, ask forgiveness of your Lord, then turn back to Him.

teach.h: RAIN, AND STRENGTH TO YOUR STRENGTH.
teach.b: He will send the sky down on you in abundant rain, and add strength to your strength. Notice who he's talking to: not weak people, but a people already well-known for strength. He doesn't tell them to give it up.
He tells them how to get more. Here, asking forgiveness isn't a loss of face. It's a source of power.
The rain matters too: for people in a dry land, rain is life.

The same promise appears in another surah, on Nuh's lips: ask forgiveness, and He will send rain and help you with wealth and children. 'Ad answer: you've brought us no clear sign; we won't abandon our gods on your word.
Some of our gods must have touched you with madness. Hud doesn't flinch. In paraphrase: I trust in God, my Lord and yours.
There is no living creature He does not hold by its forelock.

teach.h: THE STRONG WOULD NOT SAY IT.
teach.b: Commentators picture a horse led by the hair above its brow.
Every creature, every tower builder, is held. In the end, the surah says, Hud and those with him were saved by a mercy from God, and 'Ad were followed by a curse in this world.
The one thing the strong couldn't do, the thing that would have made them stronger, was to say: forgive me.

how: Muslim teachers encourage saying astaghfirullah, I ask God's forgiveness, often through the day, and cite Hud's words in 11:52 and Nuh's in 71:10–12 for the blessings tied to seeking forgiveness, including rain and strength.

o: the people of Madyan with the crooked scales
the city whose men came for Lut's guests
the mighty people of ancient Arabia Hud warned

s: Hud tells 'Ad to give up their strength
he promises asking forgiveness will add strength to their strength.
the promise of rain for seeking forgiveness also appears with Nuh
in Surah Nuh: ask forgiveness, and He will send rain and help you.
Hud asked 'Ad for a reward for his message
he says: I ask no wage of you; my wage is only from the One who made me.

games.q: you're a prophet speaking to a people proud of their strength. how do you tell them to grow even stronger?
o: ask forgiveness and turn back to God.
games.why: ask forgiveness, then turn back: He will send rain in abundance and add strength to your strength (11:52).

practice: Think of one place where you've been holding on to being right, where saying sorry would feel like losing, and notice how much effort the holding takes.
If you pray, you can say astaghfirullah slowly a few times, I ask God's forgiveness, and notice your shoulders; if not, rehearse in your mind the honest sorry you could say.

wordCard.voice: 'Ad. The mighty people Hud preached to, told that asking forgiveness would add strength to their strength. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: "strength to your strength," Hud's promise in 11:52.

carryVoice: Your line: forgiveness is strength. It's the strong who find it hardest to say. See you tomorrow.
